targetPath: /vip/interests/events-and-festivals/
kind: vip_theme
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore VIP tours for holidays and festivals"
lead: >-
  Choose a festive VIP tour of Latin America by the event itself: Rio Carnival, the Champions Parade or New Year's Eve on Copacabana. Compare not just countries and hotels, but the actual celebration, tickets, transfers and free time. Ada Tours offers short Brazilian itineraries, group journeys through five countries and private trips with nature-focused extensions.
---

## VIP tours for Carnival and New Year: choose the event before the route

**A festive journey revolves around a particular date.** An evening at the Sambadrome, New Year's Eve on Copacabana and a walk by Iguazu Falls all require different preparations. Start by deciding which event you want to attend and what participation arrangements are included in your particular itinerary. Then choose the trip duration and any additional countries.

Our VIP catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These itineraries belong to our premium selection and include a significant festive experience. The word VIP alone does not mean every journey is private: the offers include **group and private** programs. Hotel category, private guides, show seating and transfers are confirmed in the details of the chosen tour.

| Festive focus | Itinerary to compare |
|---|---|
| Carnival and Iguazu | [Rio and Iguazu, 8 days](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-8-days/) |
| Carnival and the ocean | [Rio, Iguazu and Alagoas, 11 days](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-alagoas-11-days/) |
| Champions Parade and nature | [Rio, Iguazu, Pantanal and Bonito](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-buzios-private-tour/) |
| New Year and five countries | [19-day festive itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) |
| New Year and natural areas | [16-day New Year VIP tour with Bonito](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-vip-bonito-rio-iguazu-16-days/) |

This is a starting point, not a ranking by luxury. Arrangements can differ considerably even for the same event.

## Rio Carnival: the main parade, Champions Parade and Carnival Ball

The main Carnival performances take place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Samba schools perform at the Sambadrome. The Champions Parade features the top schools from the main competition, so **a ticket to one show must not automatically be assumed valid for the other**. Check the event name, seat category, transfers and how much time is allowed to prepare for the evening.

The [8-day Carnival and Iguazu tour](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-8-days/) specifies Copacabana Palace, a Carnival Ball, a private box at the Champions Parade, private excursions and a helicopter flight over Rio. After the celebrations, the journey continues to [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), visiting both sides of the falls. These are terms of this particular journey and must not be attributed to other options in the section.

If you want to relax by the ocean after Carnival, consider the [11-day itinerary with Alagoas](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-alagoas-11-days/). It adds [Alagoas](/brazil/place/alagoas/) to Rio and Iguazu. Compare the number of seaside nights, transfers and days without scheduled excursions. Beach relaxation plays a different role here from that on a dedicated [VIP beach holiday](/vip/interests/beach-holidays/).

The [private itinerary through the Pantanal and Bonito](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-buzios-private-tour/) has another approach: following the Champions Parade are both sides of Iguazu, the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/), the clear rivers of [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/) and a finale in [Buzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). It suits travelers who want to pair festivities with Brazilian nature and are ready for several interregional transfers.

## A festival at the start of a major five-country expedition

Carnival can be the beginning of a much longer journey. The [18-day itinerary featuring the Champions Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) begins in Rio, travels through Iguazu and Buenos Aires, and continues to Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The itinerary includes [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). This is a group tour even though it is part of the VIP selection.

The [private 19-day five-country option](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) also combines Carnival with the Andean region, but in a different format. Compare the actual event dates, ticket inclusions, domestic flight arrangements, high-altitude itinerary and allocation of free days. **Similar geography does not make two tours interchangeable.**

It is especially important to allow for acclimatization: after the ocean coast, travelers reach the highlands of Bolivia and Peru. The day-by-day program and physical demands in the mountains require attention regardless of hotel standards.

## New Year in Rio: Copacabana Beach and the onward journey

You can celebrate New Year on the Atlantic coast during either a short festive break or a major journey across the continent. Unlike Carnival, the central event falls on **the night of December 31 to January 1**. Check not only that an itinerary says “New Year,” but also the exact celebration venue, arrangements for dinner or the evening and transport back to the hotel.

The [19-day New Year group tour through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) centers on celebrating at Copacabana. It then includes [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. This suits travelers who want to combine a festive night with extensive sightseeing; given the number of countries, flights, transfers and physical demands are particularly important.

The [16-day New Year VIP tour of Brazil with Bonito](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-vip-bonito-rio-iguazu-16-days/) keeps most of the focus within Brazil: Rio, Iguazu and the natural attractions of Bonito. Compare the time devoted to waterfalls, the included excursions and nights in each place rather than simply counting countries.

Another option is [New Year in Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/). After Rio, the route takes in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca. On this trip, decide in advance whether you want to move into a busy cultural program immediately after the festivities.

## What VIP means on a festive journey

**Evaluate a festive VIP tour by its actual services rather than the name of the selection.** Travelers have different priorities: special seating at a show, private transfers and extra free time, or a combination of the celebration with nature or a beach.

Before choosing, compare four things:

- **The event itself.** Which parade, ball or New Year celebration is specified? Are tickets, seat category and support confirmed?
- **Format.** Is the trip private or group-based? Which excursions are shared, and where can the schedule be adjusted?
- **Itinerary.** How many flights, hotel changes and late-night transfers fall within the festive week?
- **Terms.** Which hotels, meals, excursions and transfers are included, and which activities are optional extras?

A major [Brazil VIP tour](/vip/brazil/) and a multi-country itinerary can offer different conditions even around the same festival. Compare the specific tour pages, and use the wider [holidays and festivals theme](/interests/events-and-festivals/) to find other travel formats.

## Choosing dates and planning the festive days

Carnival follows a changing calendar: the dates of competitive parades, the Champions Parade and individual balls differ. **A month or the word “Carnival” in a tour title does not confirm attendance at the particular show you want.** Check the year, Sambadrome attendance dates and ticket conditions for your chosen departure.

New Year itineraries revolve around the fixed night of December 31. Hotels, transfers and events on that date have special arrangements. If a tour begins long before the celebration or continues afterwards, the actual number of nights in Rio matters as much as the total duration.

The Andean routes add altitude changes and lengthy transfers. For itineraries with the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) and [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), the nature excursions are more important. If relaxation after Carnival is the goal, choose an itinerary including [Buzios](/brazil/place/buzios/) or Alagoas rather than a long onward trip through several countries.

## Frequently asked questions about festive VIP tours

### Does every VIP tour include a Sambadrome ticket?

No. The selection brings together different products. The [specific 8-day Carnival itinerary](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-8-days/) describes a Carnival Ball and seats at the Champions Parade. Check the tickets and services included on any other tour separately.

### Can I choose a private tour for Carnival?

Yes. There is a [private five-country journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) and a [private Brazil itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-buzios-private-tour/). The [18-day Champions Parade itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), however, is described as a group tour. Check the format on each tour page.

### What is the difference between Carnival and the Champions Parade?

Carnival includes numerous celebrations and the main competitive parades. The Champions Parade is a separate performance by the best samba schools after the competition. Its dates and tickets are different.

### Is there a New Year trip that includes Iguazu?

Yes. The [five-country New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) combines celebrations in Rio with both sides of Iguazu and further travel through Andean countries.

### What should I choose if I want both a festival and the beach?

Consider the [Carnival, Iguazu and Alagoas tour](/brazil/tour/luxury-brazil-rio-carnival-iguazu-alagoas-11-days/) or the [private itinerary featuring Buzios](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-buzios-private-tour/). Compare the actual number of free beach days: a visit to the coast does not automatically mean a substantial beach holiday.

targetPath: /vip/interests/fishing/
kind: vip_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore VIP tours with fishing"
lead: >-
  Choose a VIP fishing tour according to time on the water, fishing location and the actual terms of the itinerary. Our selection includes a Costa Rican adventure with a full day of sport fishing in the Pacific and a journey through three natural areas of Brazil where fishing is possible during a stay in the Pantanal. Compare the itineraries, guiding arrangements, physical demands of other days and seasonal restrictions before planning your trip.
---

## VIP fishing tours: which format suits you?

**The most important question before booking is whether fishing is the main purpose of your journey or just one memorable day.** That determines which country, duration and route to choose. If you want a day on the ocean pursuing sailfish and tuna, consider Costa Rica's Pacific coast. If you would rather stay in a nature lodge, go out in a canoe, watch wildlife and fish when conditions allow, the Brazilian Pantanal may be more appealing.

Our VIP selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These itineraries differ greatly in content. The general [fishing holidays section](/interests/fishing/) lets you compare rivers, ocean fishing and specialist trips; here we focus on **combining fishing with an extensive itinerary and selecting comfortable arrangements to suit your needs**.

The VIP label means that we have included the route in our premium selection. It does not itself confirm an exclusive boat, private captain, a particular cabin category or an individual fishing guide. Check these details in the chosen tour and agree them separately when they matter.

## Two current itineraries: ocean fishing or nature lodges

| Itinerary | Role of fishing |
|---|---|
| [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | A full day of ocean fishing near Flamingo during a 13-day adventure itinerary |
| [Amazonia, Savanna and Pantanal](/brazil/tour/brazil-three-ecosystems-8-days/) | Fishing is possible during an 8-day nature itinerary; the main focus is ecosystems, animals and excursions |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ekstrim_v_kosta_rike,tour_brazil_three_ecosystems_8_days}}

These journeys are not interchangeable. In Costa Rica, a fishing day forms part of the main itinerary. In Brazil, fishing is listed among possible activities at an ecolodge. Even if both offer an introduction to fishing, the hours on the water and activities on other days are different.

### Costa Rica: a full day of sport fishing near Flamingo

On the [13-day Costa Rica adventure](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), day 10 is devoted to fishing. After breakfast, travelers head to the coast near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) for a planned trip into the Pacific. Sailfish, marlin, dorado and tuna are mentioned in the description. The possibility of catching a particular species depends on season and water conditions: the list characterizes the area, not a guaranteed catch.

Fishing is one part of a broader adventure. Before reaching the ocean, you explore the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), raft the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), visit [Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and the cloud forests of [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). The program also includes canyoning, quad biking and diving around the Catalina Islands. Fishing on the Pacuare is mentioned as another possible activity during the camp stay, but it is not a second guaranteed fishing day.

For active travelers, this makes sense: one day can be spent at sea and the rest exploring rivers, forests and volcanic landscapes. But the busy schedule is physically demanding. If rafting and canyoning do not suit you, selecting this tour solely for a single fishing outing is unlikely to be ideal. There is also a [separate 7-day fishing tour in Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) that devotes more time to ocean fishing.

The extreme adventure itinerary confirms a Russian-speaking guide, transfers, accommodation and scheduled excursions. **A private fishing vessel, particular boat model, provision of tackle and individual licenses are not separately confirmed for the fishing day.** If these are essential, agree their exact scope before booking.

### Brazil: the Pantanal, nature watching and optional fishing

[Amazonia, Savanna and Pantanal: Three Ecosystems in 8 Days](/brazil/tour/brazil-three-ecosystems-8-days/) begins around Cuiaba and travels through Mato Grosso's forest regions, the Cerrado and the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/). The itinerary combines trail walks, canoe outings, birdwatching, the waterfalls of [Chapada dos Guimaraes](/brazil/place/chapada-dos-guimaraes-national-park/) and stays in nature lodges.

Fishing is mentioned on day 6 during the stay at [Araras Eco Lodge](/brazil/place/araras-eco-lodge/), alongside a water excursion and otter watching. It does not replace the trip's central purpose: exploring nature in three different ecosystems. This is a good choice for travelers who like the possibility of fishing in the Pantanal without planning to spend their entire vacation with a rod.

The included services are regular road transfers, accommodation at three lodges, specified meals and excursions with an English-speaking guide or naturalist. International and domestic flights are extra. **Private transfers and Russian-speaking guiding are not specified.** They cannot be inferred simply because the tour appears in the VIP section.

Travel dates need particular care. Mato Grosso state imposes restrictions on recreational fishing, including a seasonal ban during fish spawning, known as *piracema*. During this period, travel through the natural areas may still be possible, but fishing cannot take place. Check the rules for the exact river section and dates before arranging your trip. Wildlife watching, too, is a natural experience without guaranteed sightings of particular species.

If your main objective is a dedicated fishing holiday in the region, compare this route with the specialist [Pantanal Fishing tour](/brazil/tour/pantanal-fishing/). That itinerary centers on fishing, while the three-ecosystem trip covers many more activities.

## What to agree for a VIP fishing trip

Ideas of a premium fishing journey differ widely. One traveler wants a spacious boat and relaxed outing in coastal waters; another wants an early departure, a long trip in pursuit of pelagic fish and several consecutive days with an experienced captain. Compare specific conditions rather than relying on the VIP label.

**Vessel and party.** Find out whether the boat is reserved exclusively for your group, how many people fish at once, whether there is a sheltered area and sanitation facilities, and how boarding works. None of these features can be assumed from the tour category.

**Guide and fishing crew.** Confirm the languages spoken by the captain and accompanying staff, who selects the fishing grounds, assists with tackle and is responsible for safety. A Russian-speaking guide on the land itinerary and a Russian-speaking fishing instructor are different services.

**Included costs.** Check boat hire, fuel, tackle, bait, licenses, meals during the outing and any harbor fees separately. The two itineraries do not fully specify these details of the fishing day. Request a final itemized list for your own trip.

**Duration and physical demands.** A whole day at sea and a short outing on a river require different preparation. Seasickness tolerance matters on ocean trips; on rivers, access to boats, heat and the accessibility of fishing stretches matter. Agree in advance what happens if an outing must be postponed due to bad weather.

**Activities for non-fishing companions.** If some family members or friends do not fish, select an itinerary that offers interesting ways for them to spend the day. The Costa Rica route includes beach days and nature activities; the Brazil itinerary focuses on excursions and lodges. But a separate activity for every companion should not be presumed included without confirmation.

## When to travel and how season affects fishing

On Costa Rica's Pacific coast, wind, rain, sea conditions and fish movements affect offshore fishing. [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) is in the country's northwest. Different species have different fishing calendars, so choose the season based on your objective rather than a generic “best month” promise. Even in a favorable season, departure depends on the weather.

In the Pantanal, water conditions are accompanied by legal restrictions. The dates of *piracema* and the rules for recreational fishing are set by the relevant authorities. As of October 2026, Mato Grosso authorities officially announced a recreational fishing ban from **October 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027** in the specified river basins of the state. Check the permitted fishing period and river stretch before planning to fish on the Brazilian tour. **The presence of fishing among a lodge's optional activities does not override the seasonal ban.**

In Costa Rica, INCOPESCA sets requirements for sport fishing and documentation. These must be checked separately for the tourist, vessel and planned type of outing. If fishing is a central purpose, tell us which fish you hope to catch and the participants' experience: it will be easier to determine whether this itinerary fits.

## Choosing an itinerary for different travelers

If you want **one full day of ocean fishing** alongside an active vacation, choose [Costa Rica](/vip/costa-rica/interests/fishing/). The Flamingo itinerary includes a specific fishing day. Before and after it, travelers explore nature areas, go river rafting and relax by the ocean.

If your main priority is **nature and lodges**, with fishing as a possible addition, consider the [Brazilian VIP selection](/vip/brazil/interests/fishing/). The specific lodge's conditions, seasonal restrictions and willingness to substitute wildlife watching for fishing are especially important.

If you want several consecutive days of fishing, compare the dedicated tours in [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) and the [Pantanal](/brazil/tour/pantanal-fishing/) with the combined VIP itineraries. That is more effective than attempting to turn a single optional outing into an entire fishing holiday.

Before requesting an offer, decide on the type of fishing, party size, preferred dates, physical demands and privacy requirements. Then you can discuss the vessel, guiding, accommodation and itinerary adjustments in detail.

## Questions about VIP fishing tours

### Does a VIP tour include an exclusive fishing boat?

This must be confirmed for the selected itinerary. Appearance in the VIP catalog does not imply a private vessel or personal captain. The offer should specify the outing format, number of participants, tackle and included costs.

### Which tour devotes a whole day to fishing?

On [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), day 10 is devoted to ocean fishing near Flamingo. On the [Three Ecosystems itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-three-ecosystems-8-days/), fishing is listed as a possible activity during the Pantanal stay.

### Can I travel with someone who does not fish?

Yes. Both itineraries offer numerous other activities. But a parallel private program for a companion must be arranged separately: the presence of nature excursions on an itinerary does not mean every guest receives a separate guide on the fishing day.

### Can I fish in the Pantanal throughout the year?

No. Mato Grosso has seasonal restrictions, including a fishing ban during *piracema*. Whether fishing is allowed depends on the precise date, stretch of water and current rules. A nature trip may be possible without the fishing outing, subject to the itinerary.

### Who is the 13-day Costa Rica tour suitable for?

Travelers who want to combine fishing with rafting, canyoning, forests and the ocean. Because the itinerary has many adventure days, it is less suited to those who prefer a relaxed holiday and fishing every day.

### Are licenses, tackle and fuel included?

The published descriptions do not confirm an identical package of fishing services for these two tours. The exact inclusions depend on the vessel, region and selected format. Agree the list of licenses, tackle, bait, fuel and other expenses when arranging your trip.

targetPath: /vip/interests/food-and-wine/
kind: vip_theme
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore gastronomic VIP tours"
lead: >-
  Gastronomic VIP tours in Latin America combine many experiences: wineries in Chile and Argentina, tasting-menu lunches in Peru, historic Brazilian coffee estates and plantations in Colombia and Costa Rica. On some itineraries, food and wine are the main purpose of the journey; on others, they form part of a wider cultural program. Choose by the actual visits, tasting formats and included services.
---

## Types of gastronomic VIP tours in Latin America

**Start with the flavors you are most willing to travel for.** A wine journey through Andean valleys, a tasting-menu lunch in Peru and a visit to a coffee-growing fazenda offer very different experiences. The actual places visited and number of food-focused days therefore matter more than the word “gourmet” in a title.

Our themed VIP catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These are current journeys with a wine or food component alongside other experiences. Some itineraries focus primarily on culture, nature or cruising; wine and restaurants may occupy only one day. **The VIP category does not automatically confirm a private tasting, personal chef at every hotel or included drinks.** Check each tour's actual program for these services.

| What to experience | Suitable itinerary |
|---|---|
| Chilean wineries | [Chile and Argentina, 17 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) |
| Wine in northern Argentina | [Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) |
| Peruvian fine dining | [Inca Deluxe, 8 days](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) |
| Gastronomy and the Belmond train | [Peru, 6 days](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/) |
| Historic Brazilian coffee estates | [Private coffee tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-private-coffee-tour/) |
| Coffee and the Caribbean | [Colombia, 10 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) |

A theme can help you find the right trips, but it does not replace the day-by-day itinerary: that is what determines whether you visit a winery, simply have dinner at a restaurant or take part in a dedicated tasting.

## Wine-focused VIP routes: Chile and Argentina

Chile's wine valleys lie in different natural settings. Near [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), you can visit the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) and [Casablanca Valley](/chile/place/casablanca-valley/); vineyard trips generally require time beyond a standard city tour. If wine is your main interest, find out whether tastings are included and how many estates can be visited.

The [private 17-day grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) includes a dedicated wine day in central Chile. The itinerary describes personalized tastings, vineyard walks and dinners, as well as arrangements for transfers to wineries. The journey then continues to Easter Island, Atacama, Patagonia and the wineries of [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/). This is an extensive private trip with a wine segment, not a compact tour solely of tasting rooms.

The [13-day Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) includes a visit to vineyards in Maipo and a Chilean wine tasting. Here the winery stop is combined with Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Chilean nature. If you want more time learning about wine production, compare the number of winery visits on the specific itineraries.

The [12-day Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu program](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) introduces a different wine region: northwestern Argentina and [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/). The tour describes a winery visit with an introduction to production, while an evening tango show in Buenos Aires includes dinner and Argentine wines. It is a good option for combining vineyards, mountain scenery and city experiences.

On the longer [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama itinerary](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), wine and food accompany a journey through Brazil, Argentina and Chile. The title indicates its themes, but compare the actual winery stops and dinner arrangements rather than forming expectations from the overall impression.

## Chile: a gastronomic lunch in Atacama and optional wine experiences

The [7-day Chile VIP tour featuring Atacama and Patagonia](/chile/tour/chile-vip-atacama-patagonia-gourmet/) has a notable gastronomic experience: a chef prepares lunch against a backdrop of highland scenery. The description also mentions gastronomic programs and Santiago restaurants.

**A visit to the Maipo Valley can be added to this tour.** That is an important distinction from itineraries with a winery visit already on the mandatory schedule. If wine tasting is your main reason for traveling, separate included events from additions requiring extra agreement.

On the extended [33-day South America journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), gastronomic experiences are combined with Peru, Bolivia and Chile. The itinerary names MIL Centro restaurant and a winery visit to VIK with a helicopter flight. Fine dining is one part of a major journey, and a substantial number of days are devoted to natural and cultural attractions. Evaluate both the memorable experiences and the total time in transit.

## Peru: tasting menus and Andean gastronomy

In [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), you can combine cultural sightseeing with an introduction to modern Peruvian cuisine. Some premium itineraries already name particular restaurants and lunches, allowing for meaningful comparisons.

The [private 8-day Inca Deluxe tour](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) includes **lunch at MIL Centro with an 8-course tasting menu**. This takes place during the visit to the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). The itinerary then continues to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Gastronomy complements Peru's archaeological and cultural experiences.

The [6-day itinerary with the Belmond Hiram Bingham train](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/) includes gastronomic dinners at Casa Moreyra and MAP restaurant, while the journey to Machu Picchu features a dining car. This is a different format: restaurants and train travel provide several distinct food experiences, but the geographical route remains Lima, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu.

When comparing Peruvian options, pay attention to **which meals are included in the price** and which restaurants are merely recommended. Even within one itinerary, the wording can refer to different arrangements on different days.

## Coffee: Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama

Coffee journeys are part of gastronomy but have their own purpose: exploring plantations, bean processing and local traditions. We have a separate [coffee tours section](/interests/coffee-tours/). When selecting a gastronomic VIP itinerary, distinguish a full day at coffee estates from a brief stop for tasting.

The [9-day private coffee tour of Brazil](/brazil/tour/brazil-private-coffee-tour/) links Rio, Iguazu and the historic [Coffee Valley](/brazil/place/coffee-valley-rio-de-janeiro/). It includes visits to [Fazenda Ponte Alta](/brazil/place/fazenda-ponte-alta/), [Taquara](/brazil/place/fazenda-taquara/) and [Florenca](/brazil/place/fazenda-florenca/) in the Rio das Flores area. Here you can discover the history of the estates and coffee production.

The [10-day VIP Colombia tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) visits the coffee region and El Ocaso farm near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). After the coffee portion, the journey continues to Cartagena and ends with time on Baru Island. If you want a closer look at growing and processing coffee, consider the dedicated [El Ocaso farm tour](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) as well as the overall itinerary.

The [12-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) includes [Doka Coffee Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/) and a cacao plantation. Its gastronomic component follows coffee from cultivation to roasting and tasting, and introduces chocolate production. A separate distinction of this particular itinerary is the flight between countries aboard a private aircraft, explicitly mentioned in its description.

On the [12-day Panama itinerary](/panama/tour/luxury-panama-12-days/), the gastronomic stop is in [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/), where a Geisha coffee plantation visit is included. The wider journey covers the Panama Canal, jungle and both coasts. If you want more coffee-focused days, compare this route with the specialist Brazilian itinerary rather than a standard city tour.

## Comparing gastronomic programs and service

Make your choice in three stages. First, set a priority: wine, coffee, one country's cuisine or a combination. Next, check how many days are devoted to gastronomy and which stops are actually part of the main itinerary. Finally, compare the confirmed services.

- **Wineries.** Are the estates, tastings and transport named? Is there a separate wine day, or simply an option to visit a wine-growing region?
- **Restaurants.** Are dinners and tasting menus included? A recommendation to reserve a table is not the same as a prepaid visit.
- **Coffee estates.** Will there be a production tour, an introduction to processing and a tasting? Or is the plantation just one brief stop?
- **Format.** A private journey and a group tour allow different degrees of freedom in arranging dinners and additional visits. Check the format of each offer.

For a broad selection of food-focused journeys without the VIP filter, see [all food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/). For the history and cultures of the same countries, explore our [VIP cultural tours selection](/vip/interests/culture-and-history/). The two sections serve different purposes: one helps select a gastronomic experience, the other a cultural itinerary.

## When to plan a wine or coffee journey

Grape harvest seasons and weather depend on the country, region and elevation. There is no single “best month” applicable to every winery in Chile and Argentina. Tasting venues and restaurant experiences may operate outside harvest season, but visiting arrangements must be checked for the specific tour.

For coffee, it matters whether you hope to see harvesting, bean processing or finished products. Seasons at plantations in [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) differ from those at Brazil's historic fazendas. For Lima restaurants, the main considerations are different: menus, visiting times and reservations. Choose your main gastronomic experience first, then arrange the rest of the journey around it.

## Frequently asked questions about gastronomic VIP tours

### Can I choose a trip primarily for coffee?

Yes. The [private Brazil coffee tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-private-coffee-tour/) reserves a dedicated day for historic coffee estates. Other itineraries, such as [VIP Colombia](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/), add a coffee farm to cultural experiences and beach time.

### Which itinerary includes a tasting-menu lunch in Peru?

The [8-day Inca Deluxe tour](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/) explicitly includes lunch at MIL Centro with 8 courses. This is a confirmed inclusion of that particular itinerary.

### Are all wine tastings included on VIP tours?

No. The [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) includes a Maipo tasting in its wine-focused day, while the [7-day Chile gastronomic tour](/chile/tour/chile-vip-atacama-patagonia-gourmet/) offers a Maipo visit as an optional addition.

### Is there a journey combining wineries with Patagonia?

Yes. The [private 17-day Chile and Argentina grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) crosses wine regions, Atacama and Patagonia. Compare the number of food-focused days with the nature portion.

### Where can I find other trips with wine and local cuisine?

Start with the [food and wine catalogs for Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/), [Argentina](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/) or [Peru](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/peru/). These show thematic itineraries regardless of whether they appear in the VIP selection.

## VIP motorcycle tours: why the route and organization matter

Traveling by motorcycle gives you the freedom to experience Brazil from the road: stop by a mountain lake, ride between historic towns in Minas Gerais and see the ocean after several days inland. When choosing a tour, it is more useful to examine **the riding stages and rental agreement** than to rely on a motorcycle photograph or VIP designation.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both current itineraries travel through Brazil, but the order of stops and terms differ. All motorcycle trips without the VIP restriction appear in the [motorcycle tours catalog](/interests/motorcycle-tours/); trips focused on Brazil are in the [country's themed selection](/interests/motorcycle-tours/tours/brazil/).

Inclusion in the VIP catalog does not mean a tour is necessarily private. One of our itineraries, for example, is designed for a group of at least 10 people. To find the right fit, check the format, guiding, transport, group size and costs beyond the base price.

## Two motorcycle routes through southeastern Brazil

### 12 days: Paraty and the coast first, then historic towns

The [12-day motorcycle tour of Brazil](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-12-days/) starts in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/). After collecting the motorcycles, the route heads to colonial [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) on the Costa Verde coast, then to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). During the second half, riders travel through [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/) and [Tiradentes](/brazil/place/tiradentes/) towards [Capitólio](/brazil/place/capitolio/) and [Lake Furnas](/brazil/place/lake-furnas/), before returning to São Paulo.

Coastal scenery appears relatively early on this itinerary, followed by longer rides through the interior. The program includes city excursions, a boat trip and days when the motorcycle can be left parked. This sequence suits travelers who want the landscape to change gradually from coastal roads to hills, smaller towns and the natural areas of Minas Gerais.

The price explicitly includes **rental of a Triumph Big Trail Tiger 900 for 10 days**, luggage transport and a support vehicle for participants traveling without motorcycles, as well as 3–4-star hotels, breakfasts, excursions and guide services. Motorcycle insurance is not included; a **$2000 credit-card deposit** is required for the Triumph 900. Road toll expenses are also listed separately. These significant costs should be checked before booking.

### 10 days: Minas Gerais first, then Rio and Costa Verde

The [10-day motorcycle tour of Brazil](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/) is intended for **a group of at least 10 people**. Departing from São Paulo, riders first head towards [Capitólio](/brazil/place/capitolio/), then continue via [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/) to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The final riding stage follows the Costa Verde coast to [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) and returns to São Paulo.

The first long stages pass through inland areas. This itinerary includes rides of approximately **460 km from São Paulo to Capitólio** and **580 km from Capitólio to Petrópolis**. Keep this in mind when choosing your pace: many hours will be spent riding, while time for sightseeing depends on road conditions and stops.

This tour includes rental of **a GS1250 or comparable motorcycle for 8 days, including insurance**. Fuel along the itinerary, toll roads, parking, a separate luggage van, a Russian-speaking guide/interpreter and an English-speaking motorcycle guide are also included. Accommodation is specified as TWIN BB. These distinctions matter more than simply comparing 10 with 12 days: the included costs and accompanying services are quite different despite the similar geography.

| Itinerary | Key distinction |
|---|---|
| [12 days](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-12-days/) | Paraty and Rio early on; Tiger 900; insurance separate |
| [10 days](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/) | Group of 10 or more; GS1250 or similar; insurance and fuel included |

## Experiences along the road

### The Costa Verde coastline

Between [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the road follows the ocean and green mountains. Stops at scenic viewpoints and visits to towns just beyond the road become part of the journey. In Paraty you can switch to walking along historic streets and around the bay, while Rio offers city sightseeing. A day with a boat outing provides a welcome break from long hours of riding.

### Mountain areas and historic towns

[Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/) and [Tiradentes](/brazil/place/tiradentes/) reveal a different Brazil. Instead of an oceanfront boulevard, you ride through hills and towns whose history is linked to the imperial period and Minas Gerais. Petrópolis offers architecture and museums, while Tiradentes invites walks through historic neighborhoods.

### Capitólio and Lake Furnas

Near [Capitólio](/brazil/place/capitolio/), the road leads to [Lake Furnas](/brazil/place/lake-furnas/) and landscapes with steep rocky shores. Both itineraries stop in this part of Brazil and allow time for activities near the water. It illustrates why motorcycle journeys need breaks: spending the entire day riding leaves less time for the natural attractions you came to see.

## Comparing rentals and support services

Confirm **the exact motorcycle model or permitted substitute**, vehicle condition, collection and return arrangements, and the rental company's age and license requirements. On a journey through varied riding areas, seat height, motorcycle weight, luggage capacity and the engine type a rider is used to all matter. The brand alone cannot tell you whether a particular motorcycle will be comfortable on this trip.

Check insurance separately from rental cost: covered risks, deductibles, deposit, who pays for damage and recovery of the vehicle. On the 12-day tour, motorcycle insurance is explicitly excluded; on the 10-day tour it is described as part of rental. This does not mean the two policies offer the same actual coverage. Request the rental company's current terms for your travel dates.

**Support arrangements also differ.** The 10-day option has a Russian-speaking interpreter and an English-speaking motorcycle guide. The 12-day option includes guide services and support transport, with the possibility of traveling without riding a motorcycle. Ask who leads and follows the group, how many riders the team supports and how assistance is arranged in case of mechanical trouble. None of this should be inferred from the VIP label.

When comparing prices, check whether fuel, road tolls, parking, meals, excursions and accommodation for any additional night are charged separately. The two itineraries have different terms; comparing two identical lists of expenses is far more useful than comparing starting prices alone.

## Riding pace, experience and season

Both itineraries require readiness for long riding days. That is especially evident on the 10-day tour with stages of approximately 460 and 580 km. Even on paved roads, a map's estimated speed is not the real average after stops, traffic, rain and riding through towns.

When choosing dates, consider rainy periods in the particular Brazilian states and road conditions along the route. Southeastern Brazil does not have a single weather pattern: coastal roads and inland highlands may have noticeably different conditions on the same day. Ask the organizer about road surfaces, expected conditions and possible replacement stages for your chosen period.

Tell the team about your experience on a heavy touring motorcycle, your maximum comfortable daily mileage and your preferred pace. If one participant rides as a passenger or some group members wish to use the support vehicle, discuss this before selecting the tour. Availability of a specific arrangement depends on the itinerary terms.

For other types of riding, including mountain roads and routes with more off-road travel, explore [all motorcycle tours](/interests/motorcycle-tours/) and [adventure journeys](/interests/adventure/). In the current VIP selection, these Brazilian routes offer two distinct ways of crossing the country's southeast.

## Choosing between 10 and 12 days

**Choose 12 days** if you prefer to reach the ocean and historic Paraty first, then gradually ride through the inland areas of Minas Gerais. Allow for the Triumph rental terms, deposit and separately listed insurance.

**Choose 10 days** if a group format with at least 10 participants suits you, and you want to start with mountain roads before reaching the coast after Rio. The included services specifically list a GS1250 or similar motorcycle rental with insurance, fuel, tolls and guides.

You can also explore [VIP itineraries in Brazil](/vip/brazil/) and the dedicated selection of [VIP motorcycle tours in Brazil](/vip/brazil/interests/motorcycle-tours/). Before deciding, compare your riding experience, group composition and the exact terms of both offers.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP motorcycle tours

### Is a VIP motorcycle tour always private?

No. Our 10-day Brazil tour is explicitly intended for a group of at least 10 people. The format of the other itinerary and any private adjustments must be agreed separately.

### Is a motorcycle included in the price?

Both itineraries include motorcycle rental. On the 12-day trip it is a Triumph Big Trail Tiger 900 for 10 days; on the 10-day trip a GS1250 or similar for 8 days. Insurance coverage and possible deposits differ.

### Which route involves more time riding?

Compare the individual daily stages rather than only the total number of tour days. The 10-day program explicitly includes long rides of approximately 460 and 580 km. On the 12-day program, review the stages between Paraty, Rio, Tiradentes and Capitólio.

### Can I join without my own motorcycle?

Yes. Both Ada Tours itineraries include motorcycle rental. Licensing, age, riding experience, deposits and eligibility for a particular model depend on the rental company's requirements.

### What if a participant does not want to ride every day?

The 12-day itinerary includes support transport for travelers who prefer not to ride a motorcycle. Availability of seats and use by a specific participant must be arranged with the organizer before travel.

## VIP nature tours: from Iguazu to Patagonia and the Andes

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The journeys feature different kinds of natural attractions: waterfalls, glaciers, volcanoes, lakes, tropical forests and salt flats. Some let you enjoy the scenery from viewpoints, while others involve extended hikes, boat trips and demanding transfers. **The VIP label does not change geography or physical demands**: a remote natural attraction remains remote even on a comfortably arranged journey.

First choose the landscape you most want to see, then compare the number of days actually spent there. Only then should you consider hotel standards, guiding arrangements, transport and potential private additions.

## Brazil: waterfalls, rivers and dunes

At [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), much depends on which side of the border your tour includes and how much time it allows for walking. The Brazilian side offers broad panoramas of the cascades, while the Argentine side has trails closer to individual falls. A visit to the second country is not automatically included simply because the waterfalls straddle the border.

The [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) offers a different experience: open floodplains, rivers and abundant wildlife. Nature activities here may include boat trips and observation. [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/) is known for clear rivers and water-based excursions, while [Lencois Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) is famous for dunes and seasonal lagoons.

For example, the [17-day journey through Brazil](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/) links several different ecosystems. It enables you to see a great variety of landscapes, but requires more flights and road transfers than a trip focused on one region.

## Argentina and Chile: Patagonia's glaciers and mountains

Around [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), the striking experience is watching the glacier's ice front. [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visiting viewpoints and walking on a glacier have different rules and physical demands.

In Chile, [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) offers lakes, valleys, glaciers and mountain landscapes. A scenic driving itinerary and mountain trekking should not be treated as equivalent services.

The [13-day Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) is useful for comparing different kinds of nature experiences. When selecting a private format, decide in advance whether you prefer more hiking or relaxed views from stops along the route.

## Bolivia: Uyuni Salt Flat and altitude

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is famous for its vast white salt flat. Its dry surface and a thin covering of water create very different views; rainfall season affects both its appearance and access to some areas.

In the highlands, consider sleeping altitude, how you feel and the length of road journeys. **A comfortable vehicle does not remove the effects of altitude.** If you want to combine the salt flats with Patagonia's glaciers, compare the [Patagonia and Uyuni tour](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) with a single-country trip: their geographical scope and flights are different.

## Costa Rica: volcanoes and cloud forests

In Costa Rica, nature itineraries often link [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Poas](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Volcanic terrain and cloud forest offer different experiences; access to trails and viewpoints may change with the weather and park regulations.

For the [classic Costa Rica itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/classic-costa-rica-san-jose-monteverde-arenal/), compare travel between natural regions, walk durations and which excursions are already included in the price. A private format can be discussed, but its actual services must be agreed separately.

## Assessing comfort on a VIP nature tour

| Question | What to check in the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | Hotels, categories, number of nights and locations relative to natural areas |
| Transfers | Domestic flights, roads, boats and journey durations |
| Guiding | Language and whether the guide is private or shared |
| Physical demands | Time on trails, elevation changes and boat conditions |
| Season | Access to natural phenomena, park trails and routes |

For wildlife encounters, see the separate [Wildlife and Safari selection](/interests/wildlife/): a view of a forest or waterfall does not imply a specialist wildlife-watching excursion. For physically active itineraries, explore [Adventure tours](/interests/adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about VIP nature tours

### Does VIP guarantee a private guide and the best hotels?

No. These conditions must be explicitly stated in the particular itinerary or agreed separately.

### Can I see a glacier without strenuous trekking?

Yes. Panoramic visits are possible around Perito Moreno. Walking on the ice and longer hikes are separate activities with their own requirements.

### When is the best time to visit Uyuni and Patagonia?

It depends on your main natural priority. For Uyuni, the condition of the salt flat matters; for Patagonia, the trails, wind and visiting season are important. There is no single ideal date for both regions.
